summary: Defines a method for negotiating and using Numbered-Mode, as defined by ISO 7776, to provide a reliable serial link for PPP. It is a standards-track proposal.

plainLanguage.summary: Normally a PPP link throws away any frame that arrives damaged or out of order. This document lets both ends agree to switch to numbered mode, where every frame is numbered and acknowledged, so nothing is lost silently. It matters most when the link compresses its headers, because losing one frame would corrupt the compressor's dictionary.

questions: how does ppp reliable transmission work
what is the ppp numbered-mode option
subtitle: How PPP can switch a serial link from best-effort frames to numbered, acknowledged ones.

tldr.problem: PPP frames over HDLC-framed links are connectionless datagrams, so a lost frame is simply discarded. Some applications need a link that does not lose frames.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a PPP configuration option that negotiates Numbered-Mode, the ISO 7776 LAPB procedure, which numbers frames and acknowledges them. The option carries a receive window and an HDLC address, and the link is brought up with a SABM frame answered by a UA frame.
tldr.outcome: A PPP link can be established in Numbered-Mode when reliability is needed, such as when header compression depends on a stream that must not lose datagrams, and the document gives default timer and retry values for it.

today: RFC 1663 is a Proposed Standard on the standards track, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The document itself marks the ISO Multi-Link Procedure as deprecated and recommends the PPP multilink procedure instead.

sections.title: Why a Reliable Link
sections.content:
By default, PPP packets over HDLC framed links consist of connectionless datagrams. If reliable transmission over the HDLC link is desired, the implementation MUST specify the Numbered-Mode Configuration Option during the Link Establishment phase.

Generally, serial link reliability is not a major issue. The architecture of protocols used in datagram networking presumes best-effort, non-sequential delivery, and when errors are detected the datagrams are discarded. However, in certain circumstances it is advisable to provide a reliable link, at least for a subset of the messages. The most obvious case is when the link is compressed. Since the dictionary is recovered from the compressed data stream, a lost datagram corrupts the dictionary, so datagrams must not be lost. Not all compression types require a reliable data stream, since the cost of detecting and resetting a corrupt dictionary is small.

The ISO 7776 LAPB can be used to guarantee delivery. This document calls that use Numbered Mode, to distinguish it from the use of Unnumbered Information, which is standard PPP framing practice.

Where multiple parallel links are used to emulate a single link of higher speed, bridged traffic, source routed traffic, and traffic subjected to Van Jacobsen TCP/IP header compression must be delivered to the higher layer in a certain sequence. The fact that the links are relatively asynchronous makes traffic ordering uncertain, and the ISO 7776 Multi-Link Procedure MAY be used to restore order. Implementation of the ISO Multi-Link Procedure is deprecated, and the PPP multilink procedure is recommended instead.
sections.plainLanguage: Ordinary PPP discards any frame that arrives damaged. Some links need better than that. The clearest case is a compressed link: the receiver rebuilds a dictionary from the stream, so one lost frame corrupts everything after it.

sections.title: The Frame Format
sections.content:
Numbered-Mode affects only the Address and Control fields. The remainder of the frame conforms to the framing in use for PPP. The Address field of the frame MUST take the value announced in the Numbered-Mode Configuration Option, and the Control field MAY take any value valid in ISO 7776.

Once the link enters Numbered-Mode, Numbered-Mode MUST be used on all frames, because some implementations do not support the Unnumbered-Information control field or the use of the All-Stations address intermixed with Numbered-Mode frames.

The frame is transmitted from left to right. The Flag field carries the bit pattern 01111110 and is one octet. The Address field is one or two octets. The Control field is one or two octets. The Protocol field is one or two octets, the Information field has variable length and the Padding field has variable length. The FCS field is 16 bits, followed by the Flag field again or by inter-frame fill or the next Address. The Protocol, Information and Padding fields are described in the Point-to-Point Protocol encapsulation document, and the FCS and Flag Sequence fields are described in PPP in HDLC Framing.
sections.plainLanguage: Numbered mode changes only two parts of a PPP frame: the address and the control field, which is where the frame number and the acknowledgement live. Everything else stays as ordinary PPP.

sections.title: The Numbered-Mode Configuration Option
sections.content:
The LCP Numbered-Mode Configuration Option negotiates the use of Numbered-Mode on the link. By default, or on ultimate disagreement, Unnumbered-Mode is used.

The option has four fields. The Type is 11. The Length is at least 4. The Window is a value between 1 and 127, indicating the number of frames the receiver will buffer, which is the maximum number the sender should send without receiving an acknowledgement. If the window is less than 8, modulo 8 sequencing is used on the link; otherwise modulo 128 sequencing is used.

It is conceivable and legal that differing window values are announced, but it is not permitted for one system to use modulo 8 sequencing while the other uses modulo 128. The rule is that a Configure-Nak may reduce the window but may not increase it.

The Address field is an HDLC Address as specified in ISO 3309. ISO 7776 specifies four of the possible values: 1 and 3 for single link operation, and 7 and 15 for the Multi-Link Procedure. Other values consistent with ISO 3309 are considered legal. Implementation of the Multi-Link Procedure is optional, so a Configure-Nak may force a change from MLP to single link mode, but not the reverse.

If the address is zero upon receipt, the receiver MUST Configure-Nak with an appropriate address. If both peers send address zero, the system advertising the numerically smaller window selects the smaller address. If both windows are the same size, a random choice MUST be made; with good sources of randomness the link converges in a reasonable time. If magic numbers have been negotiated on the link, the system with the numerically smaller magic number SHOULD specify the smaller address.
sections.plainLanguage: The option carries two numbers that matter: how many frames may be in flight before an acknowledgement is due, and which address identifies this link. Each side may ask for a smaller window than the other offered, but never a larger one.

sections.title: Bringing the Link Up and Keeping It There
sections.content:
When using Numbered-Mode, each link is established in the usual manner for the type of link. The Numbered-Mode Configuration Option is negotiated, the Magic-Number Configuration Option MUST also be negotiated, and the Address-and-Control-Field-Compression Configuration Option MUST NOT be negotiated.

Following the successful negotiation of the Numbered-Mode Configuration Option during the LCP Link Establishment phase, the system with the numerically smaller Magic-Number sends a SABM or SABM(E), and the other responds with a UA. If either the SABM or the UA is lost, this exchange may be repeated using the same parameters as the configuration exchange itself, with the Restart Timer and counter values. Authentication, Link Quality Determination and NCP Configuration follow this step.

Once the link has been established with Numbered-Mode, when re-negotiation of link configuration occurs, the entire re-negotiation MUST be conducted in Numbered-Mode. If the Numbered-Mode Configuration Option is not successfully re-negotiated, the link reverts to Unnumbered-Information operation prior to Authentication, Link Quality Determination and NCP Configuration.

Two rules handle a mismatch between what the two ends expect. An implementation that is capable of Numbered-Mode but is not currently configured for it, on detecting a frame that has a correct FCS but no UI Control octet, MUST send a DM message immediately followed by an LCP Configure-Request. An implementation that is currently configured for Numbered-Mode and receives a DM message MUST revert to Unnumbered-Information operation and immediately send an LCP Configure-Request.
sections.plainLanguage: After both ends agree on the option, the end with the smaller magic number opens the numbered link and the other acknowledges it. If one end somehow starts sending ordinary unnumbered frames, the other notices and asks to renegotiate.

sections.title: One Link, Several Links, and Multi-Link
sections.content:
On a single link, network-layer packets are encapsulated in order: header compression first, then data compression, then the Numbered-Mode header, and then the link.

Sending several connections over a single link is often called multiplexing, so sending packets from a single connection over multiple parallel links is sometimes called inverse-multiplexing. By default, PPP performs no special processing for such links. Each link is established and terminated independently, negotiates its own configuration options, and may have different combinations of options such as ACCM, Protocol Field Compression and IP-Address. This facilitates using the links simultaneously over dissimilar media, such as 56K sync with an async backup.

Every link in a single machine MUST have different Magic Numbers, and each end of every link between two peers SHOULD have Magic Numbers unique to those peers. This protects against patch-panel errors in addition to looped-back links. The distribution to each link is controlled by higher level routing mechanisms. When network-layer compression techniques such as Van Jacobsen compression rely on sequential delivery, without Multi-Link Procedure support such compression MUST be applied on a link by link basis.

This document does not offer a standard for ISO Multi-Link, but offers a method for agreeing on the addressing scheme usable with Multi-Link. Implementation of Multi-Link is not required. When the ISO 7776 Multi-Link Procedure is used, each link is established as described above, and the Numbered-Mode Configuration Option is negotiated with appropriate addresses for the Multi-Link Procedure. The distribution to each link is controlled by the Multi-Link Procedure, as is the recovery of sequence in the receiving system.
sections.plainLanguage: One connection can be spread over several lines at once. Each line is set up on its own, and each needs its own magic number so that a miswired cable cannot be mistaken for the real link. Compression that depends on order has to be done per line unless the multi-link procedure is used.

sections.title: Timer and Retry Defaults
sections.content:
The document gives guidelines for the default values of the LAPB configurable parameters.

Timer T1 is the maximum time permitted before a retransmission is started, as a result of no response to a transmitted I frame. This value must be greater than the time required for a maximum sized frame to be received by the other side of the link and for a response to be generated for it. It SHOULD be determined dynamically, based on the measured round trip time delay of the link at the LAPB level. If the system cannot determine the round trip time, the value SHOULD be set to twice the bit rate of the link divided by the maximum number of bits per frame, plus 100 milliseconds of processing time. For example, on a 14,400 bps link with a maximum frame size of 8000 bits (1000 octets), the T1 value would be set to 3.7 seconds.

Timer T3 gives an indication of the idle state of the link, and its value must be greater than the T1 value.

N2, the maximum number of attempts to complete a transmission, gives the maximum number of retransmission attempts for a given frame. If this value is exceeded, the link SHOULD be terminated. The default value for N2 SHOULD be 3.
sections.plainLanguage: Three numbers govern the retry behaviour: how long to wait before resending a frame, how long to wait before calling the link idle, and how many times to resend before giving up. The document gives a formula for the first and a default of three attempts for the last.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document is explicit that security issues are not discussed in this memo. The only related requirement it does state comes in the physical layer section: Numbered-Mode imposes the same requirements as PPP in HDLC Framing, except that implementing Numbered-Mode LAPB or LAPD requires the provision of control signals, which indicate when the link has become connected or disconnected and in turn provide the Up and Down events to the LCP state machine.
sections.plainLanguage: The document says nothing about security. It assumes the security of the underlying link and of PPP itself.

items.title: Window
items.text: A value between 1 and 127: the number of frames the receiver will buffer, and the most the sender should send without an acknowledgement.

items.title: Address
items.text: An HDLC Address as specified in ISO 3309. ISO 7776 gives 1 and 3 for single link, 7 and 15 for the Multi-Link Procedure.

items.title: Timer T3

items.title: N2
items.text: The maximum number of retransmission attempts for a given frame. If it is exceeded, the link SHOULD be terminated. The default SHOULD be 3.
